description: NASA's Earth Information Center (EIC) produces stunning visualizations of our changing planet, but presenting Earth science through visualization alone limits who can reach it. We invite you to make this complex Earth science accessible, engaging, and multi-sensory by translating sight into sound.
summary:
NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) creates remarkable visual animations that illustrate the dynamic changes occurring within our biosphere, including the 900-frame VIIRS Global NDVI daily time-series (SVS 5544). However, the exclusive presentation of complex Earth science as silent video excludes blind and low-vision (BLV) individuals and complicates the perception of subtle seasonal variations.

Earth Jukebox reimagines NASA EIC visualisations as an accessible, real-time spatial audio instrument and narrative platform. Rather than converting static images into disorganised sound, our browser-based engine samples the live 900-frame SVS 5544 video stream at 30 frames per second across a high-resolution 16×24 equirectangular grid. It distinguishes between vegetation canopy, snow and ice cover, and ocean basins, producing a continuous three-stem Web Audio synthesiser that is quantised to a C-major pentatonic scale with three-dimensional stereo panning. Complemented by WAI-ARIA grid navigation, spoken audio cues, and four carefully curated audio narratives, this innovative approach enables blind users to independently explore 2.5 years of planetary transformation.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

Earth Jukebox translates NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualisations—specifically NASA SVS 5544 (Near Real-Time Global VIIRS NDVI, Dec 2023–Jun 2026)—into a real-time, interactive spatial soundscape and curated storytelling platform designed from the ground up for blind and low-vision (BLV) accessibility.

Unlike legacy sonification tools that convert static 1D/2D number tables into disconnected sine sweeps, Earth Jukebox operates directly on NASA’s 900-frame rendered hyperwall video stream (nrt_ndvi_equi_w_dates_2048p30.mp4) through a custom browser architecture:

1. Real-Time 30 FPS Computer Vision & Palette Decoder:

As the 900-frame NASA EIC video plays, an offscreen HTML5 <canvas> downsamples each frame at 30 FPS into a high-resolution 16×24 equi-rectangular grid (384 geographic cells, 11.25° latitude × 15° longitude per cell). For any active region, the engine classifies pixels into three planetary biomes: Photosynthetic Vegetation Canopy (matched via 3D Euclidean RGB distance against the official NDVI_colorbar.png gradient), Cryosphere Snow/Ice Cover, and Ocean Basins.

2. Continuous Tri-Biome Web Audio Synthesiser:

Rather than triggering fatiguing clicks, persistent Web Audio API oscillators smoothly glide via 40ms exponential time constants (setTargetAtTime).

- Vegetation Canopy: Quantised to a 3-octave C-Major Pentatonic scale (C3–C6). Dense canopy coverage opens a biquad low-pass filter (450 Hz to 2850 Hz) and blends in a perfect fifth harmonic, making rainforests sound warm and rich while arid deserts sound muted and low.

- Cryosphere (Snow & Ice): Triggers high-register crystalline bell intervals (G5 + D6 sine shimmer). Users literally hear the boreal snowline freeze in December and thaw into forest chords in June.

- Ocean Basins: Generates a subtle 65.4 Hz (C2) sub-bass tide pulse.

- 3D Longitudinal Panning: East–west position (180°W to 180°E) drives a StereoPannerNode (-1.0 Left Ear to +1.0 Right Ear).

3. Curated Jukebox Stories & Tactile Sonic Lens:

- Jukebox Mode (Keys 1–4): Launches guided audio stories across the 900-frame timeline (e.g., Track 2: Indian Monsoon & Crop Cycle; Track 3: Sahel Greening Wave).

- Tactile Explorer Mode: Blind users independently walk across all 384 cells using keyboard arrow keys while WAI-ARIA live regions (role="grid", aria-activedescendant) and the Web Speech API announce geographic coordinates, dates, and live NDVI/snow percentages aloud.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Empowers blind and low-vision students, researchers, and museum visitors to experience NASA Earth Information Center time-series visualisations autonomously without sighted assistance. It transforms passive visual animations into an active, multi-sensory climate literacy tool where seasonal phenology, monsoon cycles, and cryosphere thaw can be heard and felt.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend & Audio/CV Engine: HTML5, CSS3 (High-Contrast Low-Vision UI), Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Web Audio API, HTML5 Canvas 2D API, Web Speech API (speechSynthesis), WAI-ARIA 1.2 Grid Semantics.

- Data Validation: Python 3, NumPy, netCDF4 (used offline to verify visual colorbar math against physical VIIRS QA-masked grids).

Originality & AI/SI Transparency Statement:

The core concept, system architecture, C-Major pentatonic spatial sonification design, multi-biome classification logic, high-resolution grid scaling, and transition to real-time 900-frame SVS 5544 video sonification were conceived and directed entirely by our team. AI tools (GitHub Copilot and Google Gemini) were used strictly as coding and documentation assistants to accelerate JavaScript/Web Audio API syntax implementation, WAI-ARIA accessibility tagging, and presentation formatting. All audio is synthesised algorithmically in real time from NASA SVS 5544 pixels.
